problem: Let $f$ be a function such that ${f}^{′}(x)=\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ and $f(\frac{\pi }{4})=0.$ Use the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ to estimate the value of $f(1).$
worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(\frac{\pi }{4})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})(x-\frac{\pi }{4}).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(\frac{\pi }{4})=0,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)=\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{sec}⁡x,$ then ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=2.$ So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=2(x-\frac{\pi }{4}).
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(1)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & ≈L(1) \\  & =2(1-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =2-\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
